layout.description: What's at the top of your cream's ingredient list? In the EU, the list is sorted by weight, below one percent the order is free, and percentages aren't shown. Here's how to read it, without anyone selling you anything.
layout.companion_text: Dewlane explains ingredients, labels and routines with sources. No product recommendations, not medical advice. Follow Dewlane for more beauty knowledge.

data.question: What's at the top of your cream's list?

beats.spoken: Every cosmetic sold in the EU comes with a list headed Ingredients. The names come from an EU glossary. That's why it says Aqua when water is meant.
The order follows weight, measured at the moment each substance is added. Whatever is at the top went into the mix in the largest amount.
But that doesn't hold all the way down. Ingredients below one percent can follow in any order. And where that line falls doesn't have to be shown on the pack.
So the list tells you which substances are in it, and which are there in the largest amounts. It doesn't tell you exact percentages. And it doesn't tell you whether a product suits your skin.

rows.text: what's there in the largest amounts

beats.spoken: Here's how to read it. The first lines show the main ingredients. Parfum stands for fragrance and aroma substances. And you can look up an unfamiliar name in CosIng, the European Commission's database.
Read the list first, then apply. Beauty knowledge, clearly explained: follow Dewlane.
